newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end mostly off on commercials, funds.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end mostly off on commercials, funds.

text.p: Late selling by commodity funds and commercials erased gains and pressured CBOT soybean futures to lower closes amid talk of heavy South American hedge selling, traders said.
Cargill Inc sold five million bushels May in the waning minutes of trade, floor sources said. Cargill Investor Services and Refco Inc were also said to be late sellers.

Traders said soybean harvest was progressing in South America and hedge selling had increased. Safras e Mercado said four percent of Brazil's soybean crop had been harvested as of February 20, about in line with average of three percent.
The May contract met with fierce resistance near $8 per bushel and the failure to pierce that key level triggered fund selling late, traders said.
Some said the weak close signalled a near-term reversal.

"We've turned the short-term trend down basis the May contract," said Jack Scoville, analyst and broker with LIT Futures. "The longer term trend remains up. We've gone to the $8 mark and found between the U.S. farmer and the South American farmer there's a good deal of product available."
Soybeans ended down 1-1/2 cents per bushel to up 1-1/2 cents with March off 1/2 at $7.83-1/4.

Bulls held on to forecasts for rains this weekend in Brazil's major soybean producing state of Parana. Traders said the rains would delay harvest progress and slow the movement of soybeans to export points.

New crop supplies were only beginning to trickle into export locations. As of Wednesday, three vessels were loading soymeal at Parana's Paranagua port and there were 14 vessels waiting to load soybeans and soymeal.
But Brazilian growers downplayed the significance of the rains, soying they should be summer showers at the worst and were not expected to cause any serious harvest delays.

USDA weekly export sales data was also disappointing. USDA said 499,600 tonnes of soybeans were exported in the week ended February 20, at the low end of trade expectations for 500,000 to 700,000 tonnes.
Volume was estimated by CBOT at 85,000 contracts, compared with Wednesday's actual volume of 70,428 contracts.
